Temporal evidence supports adding timing features inside BERT4Rec. [Session-aware BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.10851) studies session tokens, session segment embeddings and time-aware attention with few additional parameters. [TAT4SRec (2023)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1568494622009437) models continuous and discrete temporal information; its architecture differs from BERT4Rec, so it supplies design motivation rather than a direct replacement. These findings motivate testing learned time-gap attention biases or session embeddings within the existing bidirectional masked-item backbone. They do not establish gains under this benchmark.

Text evidence is less directly transferable under the no-pretraining constraint. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines item IDs with textual representations from titles, descriptions and reviews, but uses pretrained BERT and unavailable review content. Its reported benefits therefore do not validate text embeddings trained from scratch here. A compliant hypothesis: pool randomly initialized token embeddings from supplied titles/descriptions, project them into the item space, and jointly train a gated combination with item-ID embeddings under masked-target loss. Keep one BERT4Rec network and checkpoint per category, append-mask inference, and no target metadata leakage. Ablate text, timing and their combination using macro validation HR@10; semantic similarity alone is insufficient evidence of next-item compatibility.
